A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LTC-Accel work, with reliably matching main text, equations, figures and tables. v2 includes Appendices A–E; v3 ends after the references. This omission is observable in the supplied PDFs, rather than an extraction gap.

before.justification: v2 reports original image and video generation experiments in Figure 5 and Tables 1–4, plus supplementary ablations, convergence analyses and video evaluations.

after.justification: v3 retains the original image and video experimental outcomes in Figure 5 and Tables 1–4 despite omitting the appendices.

M1.justification: Section 3, Equations 1–8 and Algorithms 1–3 retain the same transition approximation, weight estimation and optional bias refinement. Removing supplementary explanations and implementation disclosures does not establish a change to the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: v3 omits the additional video-oriented WebVid-style prompt evaluation reported in Appendix D.4 and Figure 7a. The principal MS-COCO-based text-to-image and text-to-video coverage remains unchanged.

E2.justification: v3 loses the Skipping Steps controls in Tables 5/11, AYS+Skip-steps in Table 12, and the unmodified DPM-Solver++ arm of the AYS comparison in Table 8. The main comparisons with DDIM, EDM, DPM-Solver++, DeepCache, AYS and distilled models remain.

E3.justification: Retained experiments keep the same prompt counts, evaluation metrics, precision and sampling configurations. Omitted supplementary experiments remove the vBench imaging-quality/temporal-flickering evaluation and realistic-vision configurations for Animated-Diff and Animated-Diff-Lightning. These are losses of supplementary protocols, without evidence of rerunning or modifying retained experiments.

E4.justification: v3 removes matched-position skipping ablations in Tables 5/11 and 12, convergence checks across five prompt-latent pairs and two schedulers in Figure 6, and threshold, phi and bias sensitivity tests in Figure 7c–d. Figures 3–4 retain the main analyses, but substantial complementary validation disappears.

E5.justification: The mean curves and shaded bands in Figures 3–4 and initial-noise reporting in Section 4.1 are unchanged. Neither version specifies formal repeated-seed estimation, confidence levels or significance tests. The removed five-prompt convergence study concerns supplementary analysis and sample coverage.

E6.justification: Main-text numerical results remain unchanged, but distinct supplementary outcomes disappear: the skipping ablations, realistic-vision video results, convergence and sensitivity findings, and qualitative examples. For example, Tables 5/11 report seven-step DDIM ImageReward of 0.0537 for skipping versus 0.1472 for LTC-Accel; that comparison is absent from v3. Repeated appendix displays of retained results are not counted as separate losses.

T1.justification: v2 Appendix B.1–B.2 supplies the squared-error minimization derivation for w_g and the trigonometric derivation of the tau-squared error bound, Equations 9–17. v3 retains the resulting formulas in Equations 7–8 but omits their mathematical derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same claims of training-free, architecture-independent acceleration and compatibility with existing acceleration methods, including the same headline speedups. These claims are not narrowed following the supplementary material's omission.

C2.justification: Section 5 retains the same limitations concerning very few sampling steps and interval tuning. Omitted Appendix D.3–D.4 removes more specific interpretations about phi stabilizing temporal weights, large thresholds causing unstable denoising, and perceptual temporal consistency in the additional video evaluation.

D1.justification: v3 loses Appendices C–D's experiment-specific acceleration conditions, threshold guidance, bias-search settings, disclosure that optional refinement was used only with DDIM, and single-prompt weight computation/reuse with its stated overhead. This substantially reduces reproducibility information. The project-page link and code-access statement remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The same 60 numbered references and related-work discussion remain. Bibliographic differences concern line wrapping and removal of appendix citation back-references, without a substantive change in research positioning.

P1.justification: The shared main narrative is essentially verbatim, but v3 removes the entire supplementary overview and A–E section structure, including substantial explanatory prose. Main-text references to that material remain unresolved. Author-contact and publication-header edits are otherwise minor.

P2.justification: v3 omits supplementary Figures 6–17 and Tables 5–12, including analysis plots, detailed tables and extensive qualitative comparison grids. Figures 1–5 and Tables 1–4 retain their presentation and placement. Proceedings branding and pagination replace the arXiv marking.

improvement.justification: Although some appendix tables duplicate main results, v3 also loses unique ablations, mathematical derivations and calibration/interval details needed to assess and reproduce the unchanged claims. Its main text still directs readers to the missing supplement. For the supplied PDFs, this substantially weakens evidential support and reproducibility, outweighing any benefit from removing redundant displays.
